events.text: The original Tags idea retrieves knowledge through explicit weighted atom-tag and tag-tag relationships. Useful outcomes can strengthen learned weights while every atom remains independently retrievable.
Atoms encode associative weighted relationships but do not contain a fixed procedural order. Any apparent sequence comes from retrieval context rather than an ordered-step object.
Raw source content must be persisted before optional AI enrichment so a model or network failure can never discard canonical evidence.
Keep the simple atoms unchanged. If ordered problem-solving steps are later distilled by AI, store them in a separate add-on structure that references atoms instead of changing the atom graph.

Temporal History is integrated as a derived projection. Calendar summaries become auditable summary atoms with lineage to source atoms, while current-state, as-of, range, and history are conditional retrieval modes.
For the current test phase the laptop owns canonical SQLite storage. The Mac Mini performs inference and stores model files, but it does not own the ingested corpus.
Qwen3 Embedding 0.6B is selected as the initial configurable semantic embedding model because it is small and directly supported by Ollama.
Retrieval is staged: tags, lexical overlap, and embeddings generate candidates; learned relationships expand them; then the temporal lens applies the requested time semantics before evidence packing.

Relationship weights change only after explicit retrieval outcomes. Returning an atom is not evidence that it was useful, and behavioral feedback must never rewrite factual lineage or supersession links.

Harrier OSS v1 0.6B F16 replaces Qwen3 as the default embedding model. Documents remain plain, queries receive a versioned retrieval instruction, and the preprocessing profile is part of the stored vector identity.
